teams.heading: Former Bulls staff back Jake White to make Fiji surprise people
teams.body: Jake White's former colleagues at Loftus Versfeld reckon Fiji have the right man, with ex-Bulls backline coach Chris Rossouw suggesting they could surprise people. White, 62, replaces interim coach Senirusi Seruvakula and inherits a side ranked 10th that has lost four of five Tests this year. Bulls CEO Edgar Rathbone, quoted by Rapport, credits White with high-performance structures, and Willem Strauss says he leaves teams in better shape. His first match is Japan this Saturday.

lead.why: It is the only new men's 15s item in the shortlist, and it is about Fiji's own coach, so it leads over the league and women's stories.

teams.heading: Women's: England's 41-match unbeaten run ends as Canada win 24-21 in Toronto
teams.body: England women's 41-match unbeaten run, stretching back almost four years, ended in Toronto as Shoshanah Seumanutafa's late try gave Canada a 24-21 win in the WXV Global Series. Canada are the first side to beat England since November 2022, when New Zealand won the World Cup final. Head coach John Mitchell said: "We're disappointed by the result but there was some very good things in our performance. So we'll stick to our processes." The rematch in Ottawa comes before the series finishes against the USA in New Jersey.

lead.why: It is the freshest national-side result in the pack, and the club item (candidate 1) is an interview about Gloucester rather than England news.

teams.heading: Théo Attissogbe inspires club Pau to 41-17 Champions Cup win over Leicester
teams.body: France star Théo Attissogbe inspired a club win as Pau beat Leicester Tigers 41-17 in the Investec Champions Cup at Stade du Hameau. Pau trailed 10-3 early before going in 17-10 up at half-time, then scored 24 points to Leicester's seven after the break. Axel Desperes added 16 points from the boot, and Planet Rugby credited Attissogbe's brilliance with turning the match Pau's way.

lead.why: The highest-scoring new item with a France player at its centre, and the only one that is a result.

teams.heading: Jack Conan sidelined for a spell, adding to Farrell's November concerns
teams.body: Jack Conan will be sidelined after being injured in Leinster's 48-23 Champions Cup win at Clermont, the back-row having scored a second-half try before going off. Leo Cullen said: "He will be out for a little bit with that, I'd say." The timing is awkward for Andy Farrell, who already has captain Caelan Doris set to miss November's Nations Championship fixtures. Conan has not yet been ruled out of Ireland's November games. Cullen confirmed Jamison Gibson-Park came through training without major problems and could return against Munster.

lead.why: A fresh injury to a key Ireland back-row, landing alongside Caelan Doris's existing absence, is the most significant new national-side item in today's pack.

teams.heading: Scotland have scored 348 and conceded 299 across their last 11 Tests
teams.body: Across Scotland's last 11 games they have scored 348 points and conceded 299, averages of 31.6 and 27.2 a game. Put simply, Scotland have been scoring at a faster rate than they concede. The gap between those averages is 4.4 points a game. Within the same window, the biggest win was a 56-0 home victory over Tonga in November 2025, played in the International Friendlies.

teams.heading: Wales women's rugby league fall 70-6 to England on World Cup debut
teams.body: Wales's women's rugby league side began their World Cup campaign with a heavy defeat in Perth, going down 70-6 to England on Saturday. England were already 44-6 ahead at half-time. Head coach Tom Brindle named a 21-player squad with debuts for Tayla Preston and Paige Travis in the starting line-up, and Wales then face Samoa and co-hosts Australia in Sydney.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie to discuss TMO controversy at World Rugby's November meeting
teams.body: Argentina's 24-31 defeat to England is the match behind the TMO row, and the BBC's report of it ran under the headline "'Chaos' & 'comedy refereering' as England beat Argentina." Planet Rugby reports Dave Rennie will discuss the controversy at a World Rugby meeting, and quotes him: "There are lots of questions to be asked." World Rugby's review of TMO protocols remains open until it issues new guidance or concludes after the November officials meeting.

teams.heading: Les Kiss: 'None of us accept 22-0' after Wallabies' Sydney mauling
teams.body: Les Kiss was shell-shocked after the Wallabies' Bledisloe II humbling, saying of the first half: 'None of us accept 22-0.' Australia trailed 36-7 at half-time and lost 43-21 at Accor Stadium, their 13th straight defeat to New Zealand. Kiss's side had been unbeaten through six Tests, including a win over world No 1 South Africa last month, until Eden Park. The Guardian's Angus Fontaine says the honeymoon is over.

lead.why: The head coach's post-mauling reaction is the freshest unreported angle on Australia's side, and it has not been run in an earlier edition.

teams.heading: Beauden Barrett, Damian McKenzie praised by New Zealand media after Sydney win
teams.body: New Zealand's rugby writers were lavish after Saturday's second Bledisloe Test, a 43-21 win in Sydney that the New Zealand Herald's Gregor Paul called "about as good as it gets from the All Blacks". Damian McKenzie, shifted from full-back to fly-half for the first Test, and Beauden Barrett, who "wound back the clock", were among those praised, while Codie Taylor's captain's innings was singled out too. Paul also gave special praise to Dave Rennie's "vision" for the All Blacks. New Zealand led 36-7 at half-time.

lead.why: It is the freshest New Zealand-side story in the pack that is not one of the three already-reported items, and it names players and a result.

teams.heading: Club: Lions honour Hyron Andrews with tearful tribute before Champions Cup opener
teams.body: Club news: South Africa's Lions paid an emotional tribute to Hyron Andrews, the 31-year-old who was found unresponsive at the team hotel on Île de Ré on Friday, hours before their European Champions Cup opener. Players could not hold back tears during a silent observance, his number five shirt laid in front of the team and his jersey number left vacant. The Lions lost 31-14 at La Rochelle, and although South Africa Rugby said he died after falling at the hotel, no official cause of death has been confirmed.

lead.why: The most talked-about South Africa story in today's pack: a player's death and the Lions' tribute before their European opener, with no national-side item new since the previous editions.
